vars.SUB: That ratio moves before price does. Right now it's telling a specific story about who has the leverage over the next thirty days.

vars.TITLE: Selling the house together
vars.LINES:
One agent, or two?
Most couples never ask.
[[gap]]
One neutral agent:
one version of the truth.
Two agents: sometimes
lower conflict, not higher.
[[gap]]
The right call depends on
how you're [[circle]]talking.[[/circle]]
vars.NOTE: -> your attorney weighs in on anything the decree already addresses.

vars.HEADLINE:
Same Price Tag.
Different Calendar.
vars.DECK: A resale can close in 30 to 45 days. A new build runs through permitting, a builder's queue, and every change order along the way — with your rate lock on the clock.

vars.TITLE: Before the house can list
vars.LINES:
Someone passed away.
The house sits empty.
[[gap]]
Probate has to grant
authority to sign first.
That step alone takes
longer than families expect.
[[gap]]
First question: who
holds [[circle]]authority.[[/circle]]
vars.NOTE: -> confirm timing with the attorney handling the estate.

vars.HEADLINE:
Kila
[[i]]the quiet corner[[/i]]
vars.SUB: Acreage, fewer neighbors, and still twenty minutes from Kalispell — the part of the valley most newcomers never think to look at.
As the days get shorter, flat afternoon light is quietly costing listings clicks in the first 48 hours they're live.

vars.TAG: West and Company · How We Work
vars.HEADLINE:
Everyone Reads
From The Same Page
vars.DECK: Most blown deals don't fail on price. They fail because everyone was working off a slightly different version of where things stood — until one side conversation quietly drifted too far.
